card.name: Linking words in HIV/HBV warning sentences
card.fires_on: Small linking words (with, have, who) in boxed-warning sentences about lactic acidosis or hepatitis B flares. They come right before 'the use of nucleoside analogues' or 'discontinued lamivudine'.

modes.label: with after 'reported'
modes.description: The word 'with' after 'have been reported' in the lactic acidosis and hepatomegaly warning.
modes.example: Lactic acidosis and hepatomegaly with steatosis, including fatal cases, have been reported<< with>> the use of nucleoside analogues

modes.label: have/who before 'discontinued'
modes.description: The word 'have' or 'who' linking co-infected HIV/HBV patients to stopping lamivudine or FTC.
modes.example: vere acute exacerbations of hepatitis B have been reported in patients who are co-infected with hepatitis B virus (HBV) and HIV-1 and<< have>> discontinued lamivudine, a component

card.plain: It fires on the small connecting word in standard warnings about nucleoside drugs and hepatitis B flares after stopping treatment.
